Neurology · published research

Vascular parkinsonism

A non-randomized report described better long-term motor and cognitive outcomes after invasive intracerebral laser treatment, but pooled results across vascular parkinsonism and Binswanger disease do not establish a vascular-parkinsonism-specific effect.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A non-randomized report described better long-term motor and cognitive outcomes after invasive intracerebral laser treatment, but pooled results across vascular parkinsonism and Binswanger disease do not establish a vascular-parkinsonism-specific effect.

Summary of the Evidence

We identified two publications: one 2019 human comparative study and a 2023 systematic review that includes it. They represent one clinical cohort, not two independent trials. The primary paper included 62 people with vascular parkinsonism and a separate group with Binswanger disease; some reported outcomes combine the diagnoses. The intervention was an invasive transcatheter intracerebral laser procedure, not external or transcranial PBM.

Human and clinical evidence

Maksimovich reported long-term improvement in motor and cognitive measures after laser treatment compared with usual care. The paper reported outcomes across both diagnostic groups, so its pooled result cannot be assigned specifically to the vascular-parkinsonism participants. The systematic review characterized the evidence as limited and at risk of bias; it adds no new patients (Maksimovich 2019 Del Toro-Pérez et al. 2023).

Animal evidence

No relevant animal study was identified in this category.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone cell, tissue, or blood experiment specific to vascular parkinsonism was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The primary report describes red laser treatment at 633 nm delivered through an intra-arterial catheter. This route is invasive and differs substantially from non-invasive external PBM in access, dose delivery, and clinical risks. The paper does not provide a basis for transferring its result to a transcranial light device.

Interpretation

The publications support only a preliminary association for a specialized invasive procedure. Diagnosis-specific effects, independent replication, and applicability to non-invasive PBM remain uncertain.

Evidence strength in source summaryMotor and cognitive outcomes after invasive intracerebral laser: Very low
Publications and records2 unique titles

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The only primary clinical report used an invasive arterial catheter procedure and combined outcomes across vascular parkinsonism and Binswanger disease. A later systematic review summarizes the same report, so it is not independent replication. A prospective controlled study with diagnosis-specific outcomes and a clearly described comparator would be needed to strengthen confidence.
